tips.title: When someone dies at home, establish whether the death is natural or unnatural before you move anything
tips.cost: The police and the post-mortem at a government hospital are free. A private ambulance and funeral cost money.
tips.inPlainWords: If the death is expected and a doctor has been treating the person, call the doctor and the family. If the death is sudden, unexplained, accidental, suicidal or violent, call 112 and do not move the body or the objects around it. The police will register a case and arrange a post-mortem. An unnatural death needs a magistrate's inquest, and the death certificate follows the medical cause.
tips.benefit: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 requires the police to investigate an unnatural death and to report it to the magistrate. A post-mortem is required in a case of unnatural death. The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 requires the death to be registered with the local registrar. A medical certificate of cause of death is issued by the doctor who treated the person or by the hospital.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not cremate or bury before the death is registered and, in an unnatural case, before the police clearance. Keep the doctor's certificate and the FIR. A death in a hospital is certified by the hospital.

tips.title: The death certificate is the key document: the doctor certifies the cause and the municipal registrar registers it
tips.cost: The registration fee is small; a late fee applies after 21 days.
tips.inPlainWords: A death must be registered with the local municipal registrar under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. A hospital issues a medical certificate of cause of death; for a death at home, the doctor who treated the person or the medical officer certifies it. The registrar issues the death certificate, usually within 21 days. You need it for the cremation, the insurance claim, the pension and the succession.
tips.benefit: The 1969 Act requires registration within 21 days; a late registration needs the registrar's permission and a fee. The certificate is issued in Form 4 or Form 5. A hospital death is reported by the hospital; a home death is reported by the family. The certificate is the basis for the EPF, ESIC, insurance and bank claims. A corrected certificate can be issued if there is an error.
tips.sources: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs, civil registration. <https://crsorgi.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A death certificate is not a succession certificate. Keep several copies. If the cause of death is unnatural, the police and the post-mortem report come first.

tips.title: Transport, storage, and cremation of remains must be handled by funeral homes; hospital morgues cannot provide such services, and storage is generally limited to 3 days.
tips.inPlainWords: Transport, storage, embalming, body preparation, and cremation can only be done by funeral homes. Hospital morgues are not authorized to handle funeral services; they may only provide temporary storage for remains. Funeral homes typically store bodies for no more than 3 days; any longer period requires an extension request. Cremation can only proceed with a death certificate and cremation authorization document. The cremation certificate issued afterward is necessary for inheritance claims and insurance processing.
tips.benefit: Article 25 of the Funeral Management Regulations states: “Services such as transport, storage, embalming, body preparation, and cremation must be provided exclusively by funeral homes.” No other entities are permitted to offer these services. Article 24 adds: “Morgues operated by medical institutions may not subcontract or provide funeral services; they may only offer temporary storage for remains.” Hospital morgues are thus restricted to short-term storage only. Article 27 specifies: “Funeral homes may store remains for no more than 3 days; extensions must be formally requested by the family or body transferor.” Article 28 requires cremation to be performed only upon presentation of a death certificate and cremation authorization document, after which a cremation certificate is issued. Article 29 further mandates that in regions where cremation is mandatory, remains must be cremated at a nearby funeral home.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Most “one-stop” services offered at hospitals are not affiliated with licensed funeral homes. Transport itself is a standard service with fixed pricing; see Section 6 for details. Keep the cremation certificate safe — it is required for inheritance, insurance, and other legal procedures. Whether cremation or burial is mandated locally is determined by provincial authorities. Article 9 safeguards the funeral customs of ethnic minorities. Any instance of cremation being required yet burial performed, or burial outside designated cemeteries or ecological burial zones, will prompt civil affairs bureaus to order immediate correction.

tips.title: Disagreement over cause of death: request an autopsy within 48 hours and have medical records sealed
tips.cost: No cost involved. The hard part is remembering to make this request at such a time.
tips.inPlainWords: If there is any doubt about how someone died, an autopsy must be requested within 48 hours after death. Hospitals with proper freezing facilities may extend this window to 7 days. Consent from close relatives is also required for the autopsy. If consent is not given or the deadline is missed, the party responsible for the delay bears the liability for any subsequent uncertainty over the cause of death. Alongside the autopsy request, it is essential to demand that all medical records be sealed. Once the body is cremated, an autopsy becomes impossible.
tips.benefit: The time limit for autopsies is stipulated in Article 26 of the Regulations on Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes. The original text reads: “In cases where a patient dies and both the patient and medical institution dispute the cause of death, an autopsy must be performed within 48 hours after death; if the hospital has facilities to freeze the body, this period may be extended to 7 days.” In other words, to determine the true cause of death, an autopsy must be carried out within 48 hours of death, or up to 7 days if the hospital has freezing capabilities. The same article further states: “An autopsy must be approved and signed off by the deceased’s close relatives; failure to sign is regarded as refusal of consent.” If family members do not sign, it is interpreted as a refusal. It also specifies: “If consent is denied or the deadline is missed, leading to uncertainty over the cause of death, the party responsible for the refusal or delay bears all related liability.” Article 24 states that sealing and unsealing of medical records “must be conducted in the presence of both the patient and medical institution.” Both you and the hospital must be present during both the sealing and later unsealing of records.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: After this deadline passes, any later claims of “I always suspected something was wrong” will instead place liability on the party responsible for the delay. Once a body is cremated, no autopsy can ever be performed. Therefore, this decision must be made before contacting any funeral home. Details on how to seal medical records can be found in Section 24.

tips.title: After a death, register it and settle the accounts — India has no household-register cancellation step
tips.cost: The death certificate is cheap. A succession certificate involves court fees and a lawyer.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not have a household-register cancellation. The steps are: register the death, obtain the death certificate, inform the bank, the insurer, the EPFO and the pension office, and settle the estate. Surrender or transfer the ration card, the gas connection and the vehicle registration where needed. Keep the death certificate and the legal-heir documents for every claim.
tips.benefit: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 and the municipal rules govern the death certificate. The EPF Scheme, 1952 and the ESIC scheme provide for a nominee or a legal heir. The Insurance Act, 1938 and the policy terms govern a life-insurance claim. A bank account with a nomination can be released to the nominee; without one, a succession certificate or a will may be needed.
tips.sources: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A nomination is not a will, and it can be challenged by another heir. Do not withdraw the balance before the bank's process is complete. Keep the funeral receipt and the death certificate.

tips.title: Funeral services are divided into basic and non-basic categories; a list of basic services exists, with their fees set by law.
tips.cost: There is no cost involved. Just spend a few minutes before departure to review the official list.
tips.inPlainWords: Transporting, storing, and cremating a body, holding a farewell ceremony, keeping ashes in storage, and eco-friendly burial options — all fall under the national list of basic services. This also includes burial spaces provided by government-run funeral agencies. Prices for these services are strictly regulated by law; no extra fees may be charged outside this list. Before making any arrangements, be sure to confirm which services are considered basic and what the local rates are.
tips.benefit: All essential funeral services — including body transport, storage, cremation, memorial services, and eco-friendly burial — are included in the official list. Government-run funeral centers also offer designated burial plots under this same list. Their pricing follows legal standards, meaning funeral homes cannot set prices arbitrarily. Non-basic services are defined separately by civil affairs bureaus at or above the prefecture level.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities may add extra items to the national list. Always verify which services are classified as basic and what their local pricing is before proceeding. It is perfectly acceptable to want a dignified funeral for a loved one; this guideline does not discourage that. Its sole purpose is to clarify which services are fixed-price basics and which are optional extras. Once this distinction is clear, you can decide where to allocate funds — and avoid unnecessary overcharges during an already difficult time.

tips.title: If you encounter forced bundling, extra charges beyond the listed price, or a single service being split into multiple line items for billing, make a note of it and file a complaint.
tips.cost: No cost involved. The real challenge is staying diligent in the moment.
tips.inPlainWords: All these practices are explicitly listed as price violations under regulations: failing to display price lists, adding extra charges beyond the posted price, bundling funeral products and services and forcing you to buy them, and compelling you to use third‑party paid services. Splitting one service into several separate charges is also a form of price inflation. On the spot, ask for a price list and keep any receipts, invoices, and chat records. You can still file a complaint later. For price violations, contact the market regulation authority; for funeral services specifically, reach out to the civil affairs bureau.
tips.benefit: Regulations identify five categories of price violations. Four of them are: not displaying prices clearly or adding extra charges beyond the listed price — that is, no posted price list or charging more than advertised; bundling services or imposing unreasonable conditions to force a purchase — meaning you can’t obtain a service unless you buy another one; forcing or indirectly forcing you to use paid third‑party services — essentially pushing another provider’s services on you; and indirectly raising prices by re‑labeling charges — such as charging more under a different name. Additionally, it is prohibited to “split services into multiple items or expand the scope of charges to indirectly raise prices.” This means breaking one service into several line items for billing or extending the range of charges beyond what was originally stated.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Price‑violation investigations fall under the market regulation authority; funeral services themselves are under the civil affairs bureau. Ask for a price list right away, and be sure to keep all receipts, invoices, and chat records. Filing a complaint later is still possible.

tips.title: Intermediaries such as funeral service agents, vendors of funeral goods, and event planners must register with the county-level civil affairs bureau
tips.cost: There is no cost involved. All you need to do is ask whether registration has been completed.
tips.inPlainWords: Intermediaries offering services like funeral planning, procurement of funeral products, event coordination, and information consultation must register with the county-level civil affairs bureau. Those that fail to register are excluded from the official funeral service information system managed by the bureau. Availability of online lookup tools varies by region; the safest approach is to call the local civil affairs bureau directly. Any operators found to be charging excessive fees through deceptive practices or selling information related to deceased individuals will be held legally accountable.
tips.benefit: Unregistered intermediaries are not included in the official funeral service information system overseen by the civil affairs bureau. Entities that engage in fraudulent billing, pressure families into extravagant ceremonies, force acceptance of services, or illegally trade personal data of the deceased face legal penalties. Their records are also flagged within the system and made publicly accessible, ensuring transparency for all users.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: “Illegal trading of information related to deceased individuals” represents one of the most prevalent risks in this sector. It is common for families to receive numerous unsolicited sales calls shortly after funeral arrangements, often indicating that their data has been sold on. Online virtual memorial platforms are similarly subject to these regulations; Article 45 explicitly prohibits such platforms from encouraging excessive spending or mishandling sensitive personal information.

tips.title: Collect the scattered funds: EPF, ESIC, pension, insurance, bank balances and any work-related benefit
tips.cost: The forms are free. A succession certificate involves court fees.
tips.inPlainWords: After a death, the money is spread across accounts: the EPF and EPS pension, ESIC dependants' benefit, a life-insurance policy, bank balances and a pension. Each has its own form and nominee rule. Start with the death certificate and the legal-heir documents, and ask each institution for its claim form. Do not pay an agent a percentage to 'trace' the money.
tips.benefit: The EPFO pays the provident-fund balance and the EPS pension to the nominee or the family. ESIC pays dependants' benefit where the death is an employment injury. A life insurer pays the nominee under the policy. A bank releases a nominated deposit to the nominee, and an un-nominated deposit needs a succession certificate or a will. The Insurance Act and the EPF Scheme set the procedure.
tips.sources: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, nominations. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: A nominee holds the money for the legal heirs; it is not a substitute for a will. The employer may also owe a gratuity or leave encashment. Keep the acknowledgement for every claim.

tips.title: Relatives of the deceased may request access to, copies of, corrections to, and deletion of their personal information
tips.cost: No cost involved. Only if the platform refuses cooperation would legal complaints or lawsuits be necessary.
tips.inPlainWords: After a person passes away, their close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, ask the platform to access, copy, correct, or delete that person’s personal information. If the platform denies such requests, it must provide a valid reason. Legal action in court is also an option. One exception applies: if the deceased made prior arrangements—such as designating a successor to their account or expressing clear intentions—those instructions must be followed.
tips.benefit: The law explicitly states that upon a person’s death, their close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, exercise rights such as accessing, copying, correcting, and deleting the deceased’s personal information. In other words, they may request the platform to provide access to this data, make copies, correct any errors, or remove it entirely.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: The legal text includes a clause stating “except where the deceased made prior arrangements.” This means that if someone designated a successor to their account or left explicit instructions, those must be honored. Therefore, while still alive, it’s advisable to document where one’s account credentials are kept, as explained in Section 17. Note also that account deactivation and deletion of personal information are two distinct processes, as discussed in Section 14.

tips.title: Heirs pay the deceased's debts only out of the estate they inherit, not from their own money
tips.cost: A probate or a succession certificate costs money; a lawyer is advisable for a large estate.
tips.inPlainWords: Under Indian succession law, an heir is liable for the deceased's debts only to the extent of the estate received. If the debts exceed the assets, the heir can refuse the inheritance or let the estate be administered by the court. A secured creditor can enforce the mortgage against the property. A formal renunciation or a probate may be needed.
tips.benefit: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 and the personal laws govern inheritance; the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 governs the execution of a decree against the estate. A creditor can sue the legal representative, but recovery is limited to the estate's value. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 provides a route where the estate is insolvent. A will can name an executor.
tips.sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India. <https://ibbi.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not sign a personal guarantee for the deceased's debt. A joint loan may make the surviving borrower liable. A secured asset can be repossessed even if the heir refuses the inheritance.

tips.title: Not every inheritance needs probate; a nominated bank deposit can be released on the bank's form
tips.cost: A nomination claim is free. A succession certificate or probate involves court fees and a lawyer.
tips.inPlainWords: Probate is not mandatory for every estate. A bank deposit with a valid nomination can be released to the nominee on the bank's claim form with the death certificate. Without a nomination, the bank may ask for a succession certificate, a probate or an indemnity, depending on the amount. A will still needs probate if it deals with immovable property in some jurisdictions.
tips.benefit: The RBI's customer-service rules and the bank's nomination scheme allow a nominee to receive a deposit. The Indian Succession Act, 1925 requires probate for a will in some cases, and the state rules vary. A succession certificate is issued by a civil court for debts and securities. A small estate may be settled with an affidavit and an indemnity, subject to the bank's policy.
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India, customer service. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A nominee is a trustee for the legal heirs, not necessarily the owner. A joint account with a survivorship clause passes to the survivor. Do not withdraw before the bank completes its process.
